chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Abi Wallad al-Hannat, who said:

I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a Muslim man who intentionally killed a Muslim, and the slain person had no heirs among the Muslims except heirs from among the Ahl al-Dhimmah from his relatives. He said:

"It is upon the Imam to present Islam to his relatives from the people of his household. So whoever among them accepts Islam, then he is his heir; the killer is handed over to him. If he wishes, he may kill; if he wishes, he may pardon; and if he wishes, he may take the diyah. But if none of them accepts Islam, then the Imam is the guardian of his affair. If he wishes, he may kill; and if he wishes, he may take the diyah and place it in the Bayt Mal of the Muslims, because the liability concerning the slain person was upon the Imam, and likewise his diyah belongs to the Imam of the Muslims."
I said to him: What if the Imam pardons him? He said: "It is only the right of all the Muslims, and it is only upon the Imam either to kill or to take the diyah, and he has no right to pardon."

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: non-Muslim protected subjects under the Islamic covenant, mentioned here as relatives of the slain person
key_terms.الدِّيَةَ: blood money paid in compensation for the killing
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam as the authority who assumes legal guardianship when no eligible Muslim heir exists
key_terms.الْقَاتِلُ: the killer who is handed over to the wali for legal decision
key_terms.بَيْتِ مَالِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the public treasury of the Muslims where the diyah is placed in this case
key_terms.حَقُّ جَمِيعِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ: a right belonging collectively to all Muslims, restricting the Imam from personal pardon
key_terms.وَلِيُّهُ: his legal guardian or heir with authority over the case

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a Muslim murder victim has no Muslim heirs except dhimmi relatives?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal ruling regarding intentional killing when the slain Muslim has no Muslim heirs except non-Muslim relatives from among Ahl al-Dhimmah. The Imam must first offer Islam to those relatives; if one of them accepts Islam, he becomes the wali and may choose qisas, pardon, or diyah. If none accepts Islam, the Imam assumes guardianship and may enforce qisas or take the diyah for the Bayt Mal, but he may not pardon because the right belongs to the Muslims collectively.
